title: Geofenced Evidence Bundler for Dedicated Tenant Audits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a scheduled, verifiable evidence bundler that collects geolocation-anchored artifacts for Dedicated tenants and packages them into audit-ready archives. The bundle (GEB) should include node residency metadata, network topology snapshot, tenant routing headers, KV-cache provenance, retention policy markers, and signed manifests. Bundles must be exportable on-demand and via automated retention reports for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Daily bundle generation runs for each Dedicated tenant with a residency constraint and produces a signed archive and machine-readable manifest.
Manifest includes: tenant id, node ids and locations, instance image/tags, timestamps, hashes of included artifacts, and retention TTL metadata.
Signer service verifies and signs manifests using KMS-backed keys; signature timestamp is recorded and verifiable.
Bundles are stored encrypted, retained according to tenant-configured retention settings, and can be exported to a secure customer S3 or SOC2 audit bucket.
Console shows per-tenant last-bundle status, size, and retention expiry; export links respect RBAC and are time-limited.
Automated evidence report can be generated for a given date range and includes a human-readable summary plus machine manifest for auditors.
End-to-end integration tests that simulate node reprovisioning and show that bundles capture residency drift within 1 hour.
Cost budget: average storage per tenant remains within projected S3 costs documented in the PRD.
technical_notes: Bundle format: compressed tarball + JSONL manifest (GEB-1). Rationale: streamable creation and easy verification of individual artifact hashes.

Artifacts to include: agent heartbeat logs (last 24h), orchestration placement events, node metadata (AZ/region, host id, GPU type), routing headers for tenant requests, KV-cache snapshot metadata (not raw tokens), and retention policy record.
We will not include raw customer request payloads; only metadata and hashes/pointers to facilitate privacy and PII avoidance.
Signing: residency-signer service will call KMS/HSM to produce an RSA/ECDSA signature over canonicalized manifest. Signature scheme documented in design doc.
Storage: per-tenant encrypted prefix in internal S3; option to auto-copy to customer-managed bucket using cross-account replicator for exported evidence.
Retention: TTL labels in manifest and lifecycle rules on object storage enforce deletion; retention overrides allowed by legal hold flag.
Performance: bundle generation is I/O-bound; use streaming hash (blake3) and parallel compressor to keep wall time under 3 minutes for 1GB of artifacts.
Operational: bundler runs as a fingerprinted Kubernetes CronJob in Dedicated control plane; uses node affinity to collect local node facts when possible.
Discovery: geofencing uses provider metadata + node binding table; a fallback of IP-to-region lookup is applied when provider metadata missing.

decisions: Use JSONL manifest instead of a single large JSON to support streaming verification and partial rehydration.
Sign manifests with a tenant-scoped signing key derived from KMS wrapped keys (residency-signer) to enable per-tenant revocation and auditability.
Do not persist raw request bodies or model outputs in bundles by default; include hashes and pointers only. This keeps PII exposure low while still providing cryptographic evidence.
Bundle generation frequency: default daily; support on-demand and hourly for high-risk tenants (configurable).
risks: Large tenants may produce >10GB/day of artifact metadata; storage costs could spike if retention not tuned.
Signer key management complexity: key rotation must be coordinated with archived manifests so old signatures remain verifiable.
Network partitions may delay bundle collection leading to incomplete daily bundles; need clear indicators in manifest for missing artifacts.
Export to customer-managed buckets requires cross-account permissions which have operational support overhead and potential security pitfalls.
dependencies: SEC-128 (security policy review for evidence exports)
